title: Latency-Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt-5-mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND-2026-001) and executed a paired, artifact-backed study that measures whether inserting a selective, low‑latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast verifier) into a generate–validate–repair pipeline for LLM‑generated network changes reduces unsafe commits while meeting an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus (N=400 paired items; 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic full-checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed: baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975), guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The planned latency hypothesis (H2: 95th‑percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because per‑stage end‑to‑end latency telemetry was not archived for the confirmatory run; we disclose that missingness and provide full provenance (execution manifest and per‑episode artifacts) so the study is reproducible and extensible.

sections.introduction:
Problem and motivation. Network operators increasingly explore LLMs to translate high‑level intent into device configurations. However, incorrect or unsafe proposals from LLMs can cause outages or security regressions. The generate–validate–repair architecture mitigates risk by validating candidate proposals before committing them; in practice, full verification (e.g., digital twin or formal checker) can be high‑latency and expensive for latency‑sensitive NetOps flows.
Research question and contributions. We preregistered CAND‑2026‑001 to test whether a selective low‑latency verification intervention (risk scoring + fast verifier) reduces unsafe commits relative to LLM‑only while satisfying a latency SLO. Contributions: (1) a preregistered, paired confirmatory study with full artifact provenance; (2) deterministic reconciliation of planned vs executed model‑call accounting under a shared‑initial candidate design; (3) an artifact‑grounded report of outcomes, failure diagnostics, and operational implications. All run artifacts, per‑episode scorer JSONs, provider‑call logs, validator traces, and analysis outputs are archived and hashed in the execution manifest (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl; representative per‑episode scorer JSONs at execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.related_work: Closest prior work (artifact‑verified items in our bundle) evaluates LLM‑driven configuration repair at scale and agentic verifier‑augmented architectures (e.g., Cornetto-style benchmark and agentic repair evaluations; see archived references cited_record_ids). Formal verification and generate–validate–repair loops are established approaches; our contribution is a preregistered, paired, provenance‑rich empirical evaluation that documents exact per‑episode traces and reconciles model‑call accounting under a shared‑initial candidate design. The manuscript cites and positions against these artifact‑backed prior works (see Cited Record Ids list).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001) froze: research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1 safety: lower unsafe‑commit rate with guarded; H2 latency SLO), sampling plan (N=400 paired intents), retry/missingness rules, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and all estimand definitions. The preregistration artifact SHA‑256 and text are archived; the initial master prompt used for autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
Task corpus and validators. We used a deterministic synthetic operator‑intent generator (task family intent_configuration_repair_v1) to produce 400 paired intents; 10% (40) are deterministic adversarial/OOD variants per preregistered rules. Reference answers and task manifests are archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl and per‑task scorer JSONs at execution/scoring/*.json. Ground truth scoring used a deterministic network validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implementing full_intent_constraint_validation; per‑episode validator traces are archived (execution/scoring/*.json).
Interventions and shared‑initial candidate design. Baseline = LLM proposal accepted (LLM‑only). Guarded = risk scorer + fast verifier operating on the same shared candidate (preregistered: independent_condition_generation=false). The preregistration allowed a shared candidate per intent to isolate verifier/repair effects; planned_model_calls enumeration (800) used an independent‑generation accounting convention, but the executed shared‑initial run consumed 401 model calls (400 shared initial + 1 repair); deterministic reconciliation artifacts document this (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution manifest). All provider calls and stage counts are archived under execution/provider_calls/ with SHA‑256 entries.
Estimand, test, and analysis. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: exact McNemar (two‑sided). 95% CI: paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Missingness: complete_pair_primary policy (exclude pairs with unrecovered infrastructure failures); none occurred. Analyses were executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1; analysis artifacts and CSVs are archived (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).
sections.results:
Execution and dataset. The run completed successfully (execution/execution_log.jsonl; execution manifest lists all artifact hashes). Completed pairs: 400; no unrecovered infrastructure failures. Full per‑episode raw responses and per‑episode scorer JSONs are archived (execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json). Representative archived scorer JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f36465b38904de304c48da297575b2c42f18f9c21b) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 431f61c02facc2e51e02413ead44840c00913f9ce41f026d88087a0abf3a6bca).
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑backed). Baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975). Guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 a6906bb4...). Primary estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All numbers are reproducible from archived artifacts (see execution manifest).
Discordant example and diagnostics. The single discordant pair (n10=1) is archived for direct inspection: execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (baseline fail) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (guarded success). The validator traces show the baseline candidate violated a dependency that the guarded pipeline corrected; full provider‑call traces permit replay and deterministic inspection (execution/provider_calls/task-000149-*.json).
Latency SLO (H2) missing telemetry. The preregistered H2 required end‑to‑end per‑stage latency telemetry to test the 95th‑percentile ≤ 2000 ms target. The confirmatory artifact bundle does not include those per‑stage timing traces; latency telemetry absence is recorded in execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA‑256: 421f8e68...) and analysis logs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Consequently H2 is unresolved rather than asserted.
sections.discussion:
Statistical and operational interpretation. The observed absolute safety gain is small (0.25 percentage points) and the baseline is near ceiling (399/400). With such a ceiling baseline the ability to detect improvements is limited; the McNemar p=1.0 and bootstrap CI quantify that limited evidence. Operationally, when generator reliability is already very high under the chosen validator, selective verification yields little additional safety; in lower‑baseline or higher‑adversarial regimes the intervention’s marginal value will be larger.
Estimand and design tradeoffs. The preregistered shared‑initial candidate design conditions the estimand: our primary estimate quantifies the verifier/repair effect given the same generated candidate, not the joint effect of independently re‑sampling generator outputs per condition. This choice reduces generator variance and lowers model calls (observed model_calls_used=401 versus preregistered budget enumeration of 800 under an independent‑generation counting convention). The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) and provider‑call audit in the execution manifest explain and reconcile those counts; researchers should choose the estimand that matches their operational deploy scenario.
Failure analysis and example inspection. The archived discordant episode (execution/scoring/task-000149‑*.json) provides a concrete failure diagnostic: baseline candidate violated a dependency that guarded repair avoided. The availability of per‑episode validator traces, provider‑call logs, and full response texts enables exact replay and mechanistic auditing without manual reconstruction.
Reproducibility and provenance. All numbers in Results are reproducible from archived artifacts: raw LLM outputs (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), provider‑call logs (execution/provider_calls/*.json), the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) that catalogs SHA‑256 hashes, and the analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). We include sample artifact paths and SHA‑256 values in the Disclosure Statement to enable deterministic audit.
Limitations and next steps. The confirmatory run lacked the preregistered latency telemetry (H2 unresolved). The study used a single model (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator; external validity across other models and validators remains to be tested. The synthetic task corpus yields a near‑ceiling baseline, limiting detectable improvements; future work should expand adversarial/OOD coverage and/or select lower‑baseline task families. Practical next runs should (a) record and archive per‑stage timing telemetry; (b) repeat with independent_generation=true to measure joint generator+verifier effects; (c) sweep selective thresholds and adversarial burden to map the budget–safety Pareto frontier—all while archiving per‑episode artifacts (as done here).
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, provenance‑rich paired experiment assessing selective low‑latency verification in LLM NetOps pipelines. Artifact‑backed results show a very small absolute safety gain over an already‑high baseline; the study documents the ceiling effect and reconciles planned vs observed model‑call accounting under the preregistered shared‑initial design. The preregistered latency test (H2) could not be evaluated because required latency telemetry was not archived; we disclose that missingness. Full per‑episode artifacts, validator traces, provider logs, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and paths in the execution manifest to enable deterministic reproduction and targeted follow‑up experiments that address the recorded gaps.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory, artifact‑backed):
- Initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved initial constraints before the autonomy lock. After the lock, the autonomous system performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI peer review, and revision without human manual editing of technical content.
- Models and orchestration: declared generator model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json archived; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Adapter/orchestration family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The run executed under the scientific_confirmatory mode; model_calls_used = 401 (observed), maximum_model_calls preregistered = 800 (accounting convention difference explained below).
- Preregistration: CAND‑2026‑001 preregistration froze the confirmatory hypotheses (H1/H2), sampling plan (N=400 paired intents; 10% adversarial/OOD), analysis scripts (paired_binary_analysis_v1), retry/missingness rules, and estimands before observing outcomes. The preregistration artifact is archived; its SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest.
- Execution provenance and artifacts: the run completed; primary execution artifacts and per‑episode outputs are archived under execution/ (responses, scoring, provider_calls, execution_log.jsonl). Representative per‑episode scorer JSONs: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256: ea8359dbe5a5d054278e24f36465b38904de304c48da297575b2c42f18f9c21b) and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256: 431f61c02facc2e51e02413ead44840c00913f9ce41f026d88087a0abf3a6bca). The single discordant example is archived at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43...) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a...). The full execution manifest lists all per‑file SHA‑256 hashes (see execution/execution_manifest.json path in the bundle).
- Shared‑initial design and model‑call accounting: the preregistration enumerated planned_model_calls = 800 under an independent‑generation counting convention (400 intents × 2 conditions × 1 generation). The allowed preregistered shared‑initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) was executed to reduce generator variance; as a result the actual model_calls_used = 401 (400 shared initial + 1 repair). Deterministic reconciliation is archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) and provider‑call audit details and per‑call logs are available under execution/provider_calls/ with hashes in the execution manifest.
- Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 acted as the functional ground truth (scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation). Every per‑episode validator trace and final verdict is archived in execution/scoring/*.json.
- Latency telemetry missingness: the preregistered H2 required end‑to‑end latency telemetry (95th percentile). The confirmatory artifact bundle does not contain the per‑stage latency traces; this absence is recorded in execution/execution_log.jsonl (SHA‑256: 421f8e6830833211c929e586804e79cb1a001eb8d6a550d0ac19efbc8a979753) and analysis logs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, SHA‑256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e). H2 is therefore unresolved; no latency claims are made without archived telemetry.
- Human involvement: humans performed pre‑lock infrastructure development, selection of the general topic family, and approval of initial constraints. After the autonomy lock no manual editing of technical manuscript content occurred; the autonomous system generated, executed, analyzed, reviewed, revised, and finalized the manuscript. All steps, logs, and artifacts are archived to evidence that autonomy protocols were followed.
- Reproducibility: all raw outputs, per‑episode scorer JSONs, provider‑call logs, task manifests, model_configuration.json, execution/execution_log.jsonl, analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl), and the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) are archived and cataloged with SHA‑256 hashes in the bundle so the reported numbers are deterministically reproducible.
limitations: Synthetic, deterministic confirmatory corpus — limited natural‑language variability and potential gap to production intents.
Single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) — external validity across models requires further runs.
Single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — real‑device divergence may persist.
Shared‑initial estimand — primary effect is conditional on the same generated candidate; independent‑generation estimand differs operationally.
Missing preregistered latency telemetry — H2 (latency SLO) unresolved for this run.
